OpenAI announced plans to retire Custom GPTs and move their specialized workflows to a new plugin architecture for ChatGPT and Codex.
Meta introduced Muse Glimmer, an open-weight AI model designed to run on consumer hardware.
Microsoft unveiled Frontier Company and announced a $2.5 billion investment focused on helping enterprises use AI models.
Valar Atomics and Nvidia announced a partnership to explore AI data centers powered directly by advanced nuclear energy; the article describes it as an industry first.
Valar Atomics and Nvidia are considering a 30-megawatt, nearly waterless Utah data center using the Ward250 reactor and Nvidia cooling technology.

Isaiah Taylor said the reactor’s fuel contains enough energy to drive a car around Earth 7,000 times.

The Information reported on 2026-07-01 that Firmus and Sharon AI had joined NVIDIA’s program and that three executives with NVIDIA business ties confirmed the arrangement.

Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 GB300 GPUs; Firmus is constructing a Batam campus planned for up to 360 MW and 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.
A data center executive characterized NVIDIA’s deals as “killing two birds with one stone.”
An unnamed data center executive said a NVIDIA commitment to purchase unsold compute capacity would address both GPU and data-center financing problems.
moomoo.com reported on 2026-07-01 that Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Oracle, Meta, and Google purchase the majority of NVIDIA’s chip output.

Palantir CEO Alex Karp argued that OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly lack measures to protect clients’ IP.

Palantir said its system supports secure, air-gapped AI deployment, customer customization and ownership of model weights, and security and audit capabilities for sensitive deployments.
Nvidia and Palantir said their combined open models and software provide greater transparency, customization, and cost efficiency than closed AI models.
Nvidia said it is looking to give developers token credits in exchange for a share of their future sales; no amount or timeframe was specified.

Nvidia CFO Colette Kress said Nvidia would connect AI data centre operators with cloud service providers to simplify access and establish a recurring earnings stream; no amount or timeframe was specified.

Verkada said it is scaling its physical AI platform across more than 2.4 million devices globally and announced a technical collaboration and investment from NVIDIA.
Verkada said NVIDIA joined as a new investor; it said Alphabet's CapitalG made a strategic investment at the end of 2025.
Verkada CEO Filip Kaliszan said Verkada's platform covered more than 2.4 million devices, 170 countries and 30,000 organizations as of July 1, 2026.
Verkada said its collaboration with NVIDIA was advancing video search, multimodal embeddings, vector retrieval and synthetic data generation for its intelligent video analytics.
Verkada said it used NVIDIA Cosmos, NVIDIA Physical AI Data Factory and NVIDIA accelerated computing to accelerate model training and inference.
Verkada said its AI-powered search mAP for spatial-temporal understanding improved by 68% since its collaboration with NVIDIA began.
Verkada said more than 30,000 organizations in 170 countries, including more than 100 Fortune 500 companies, used its physical security platform.
NVIDIA said 12 new games, including Monopoly: Star Wars Heroes vs. Villains, would join GeForce NOW in July 2026.
NVIDIA offered a $35 saving on a 12-month GeForce NOW Performance membership during the Summer Sale.
NVIDIA offered a $70 saving on a 12-month GeForce NOW Ultimate membership during the Summer Sale.
An unnamed GeForce NOW member said a year of Ultimate reduced their calculated monthly cost from roughly 29 CAD to 17 CAD.
Ajay K. Puri notified NVIDIA on June 28, 2026, of his intention to retire as EVP of Worldwide Field Operations when his successor begins employment.
NVIDIA said Ajay K. Puri is expected to remain in a senior advisory role during the transition to his successor.
NVIDIA appointed Nicholas Parker as EVP of Worldwide Field Operations on July 1, 2026, with his employment anticipated to begin August 24, 2026.
NVIDIA said Nicholas Parker's annual base salary will be $1,000,000.
NVIDIA said Nicholas Parker will receive a $5,000,000 sign-on bonus.
NVIDIA said Parker will be eligible for target annualized cash variable compensation of $1,500,000, prorated for his time worked in FY2027.
NVIDIA said Parker will receive new-hire RSUs with a target value of $35,000,000, vesting approximately over four years under its standard schedule.
NVIDIA said Parker will receive performance-based RSUs with a $5,000,000 target value, eligible to vest based on relative total shareholder return over three years.
NVIDIA said Parker will enter into its indemnity agreement, under which the company would cover specified expenses and other amounts arising from certain proceedings connected with his officer role.

Under the announced arrangement, Nvidia receives revenue from product sales and cloud operations as AI cloud companies provide Nvidia-powered services to end customers; no amount or period was specified.
Nvidia CFO Colette Kress described the arrangement's income as a “recurring, usage-linked earnings stream”; no amount or period was specified.
The offering includes token credits that let startups access compute resources without upfront capital outlays; no amount or period was specified.
Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs; no deployment date was specified.
Firmus Technologies is developing a campus in Batam, Indonesia, planned for capacity of up to 170,000 Nvidia GPUs and 360 megawatts of power; no completion date was specified.
Nvidia said Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Together AI represent the type of customer its program is designed to serve; no amounts or period were specified.

Sharon AI cofounder and CEO James Manning described the collaboration with Nvidia as a pivotal moment for Sharon AI's effort to deliver sovereign, large-scale AI compute infrastructure; no figure or period was specified.
Firmus Technologies co-CEO Tim Rosenfield said AI-native companies need scalable, energy- and cost-efficient compute infrastructure to compete globally; no figure or period was specified.

Nvidia characterized the program as a response to AI demand shifting from model development toward production inference workloads requiring continuously operating infrastructure at scale; no figure or period was specified.

Nvidia said emerging AI companies have historically had limited access to capital-intensive compute resources and that even long-term commitments have been insufficient to unlock financing; no figure or period was specified.
Nvidia said on 2026-07-02 that it was introducing a partnership program to connect AI startups with computing infrastructure through its AI cloud service provider network.
Under the program, cloud-based AI firms, model builders and other enterprises will share product and cloud revenue with Nvidia; no amount or period was specified.
Sharon AI said it would deploy up to 40,000 Nvidia GPUs; Firmus Technologies said it was building a Batam data center expected to reach 360 MW and house up to 170,000 Nvidia GPUs.
CNBC reported in January that OpenAI had entered deals involving share purchases or contemplated investments from Amazon and AMD; the item gives no deal sizes.

Nvidia said it intended to use proceeds from the debt offering for general corporate purposes, including repaying and refinancing existing debt; no amount or period was specified.
Nvidia is reported to backstop neocloud companies financially in exchange for a share of their revenue; no amount or period is specified.
Nvidia is reported to agree to rent back unused GPUs at a fixed rate as part of the backstop; the rate and period are unspecified.
DatacenterDynamics reported on 2026-07-02 that Firmus and Sharon AI had adopted Nvidia's offer; no contract amount or date was specified.
DatacenterDynamics reported that Firmus was deploying 170,000 GPUs in Batam, Indonesia, and Sharon AI was deploying 40,000 GB300 GPUs; no completion date was given.
Nvidia said its new model lets AI clouds procure Nvidia infrastructure using revenue-sharing and credit support for AI-native, enterprise, and ISV customers; no amount or period was specified.
Nvidia said it would earn standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on capacity supported through the partnerships; no amount or period was specified.
Nvidia said the structure would provide it with recurring, usage-linked earnings; no amount or period was specified.
DatacenterDynamics reported that Nvidia signed an agreement with CoreWeave in September 2025 with an initial value of $6.3 billion.
DatacenterDynamics reported that Nvidia's deal with Lambda was valued at $1.5 billion; no signing date was stated here.

Microsoft unveiled the $2.5 billion Microsoft Frontier Company initiative on Thursday, to embed AI engineers inside customers; Rodrigo Kede Lima will lead it.

Firmus is building a DSX-aligned campus in Batam expected to scale to 360 MW and house up to 170,000 Nvidia GPUs.
